name: Gifts of the River: Great Rivers and the Peoples They Fed
description: The Nile, Tigris, Euphrates, Indus and Yellow River watered fields, cities and kings. See what grew beside them and how people learned to master floods.

checkpoints.name: First fields
checkpoints.note: Farmers learned to use river floods. Irrigation, the Nile's yearly rise and the rivers of Mesopotamia fed Sumer, Egypt's pyramid builders and the cities of the Indus, along with writing in clay and hieroglyphs.

checkpoints.name: Kings and canals
checkpoints.note: Water lifts such as the shaduf spread farming. Hammurabi's laws governed Babylon, Assyria built Nineveh, Kush rose beside the Nile, and the first emperor and his heirs dug canals linking China's rivers.

checkpoints.name: Floods and fortunes
checkpoints.note: Rivers kept shaping history. The Grand Canal tied China's north and south, and the Yellow River, nicknamed China's Sorrow, broke its banks again and again, most destructively in 1887.

checkpoints.name: Dams and drained seas
checkpoints.note: Great dams such as Aswan and Three Gorges tamed floods and made power, while the 1931 China floods showed what was at stake. Drawing off rivers also shrank the Aral Sea.
